build.reason: build.sh runs a default configure, builds libz.a, then compiles each *_fuzzer.c against it. All APIs the harness uses are declared in zlib.h.

input.reason: In case 4, whences has 5 elements but is indexed with (*data)%6, so index 5 reads out of bounds. Input bytes 00 04 05 reach it.

lifecycle.reason: Case 21 calls gzclose_r and then sets file to NULL, even if the handle is in write mode. Whether gzclose_r frees a write handle is not supplied.

control_flow.reason: The op loop dispatches on byte%26 to every case. Each API used checks for a NULL file, so the loop works even when gzopen fails.

missing_information: gzclose_r body (gzclose.c / gzread.c) for the lifecycle of write handles

accepted.requirement: The harness's seek operation must choose whence from a valid index into its own whences array.
accepted.failure_condition: Input 00 04 05: mode_sz=2, so the copy into mode does not advance data. The op byte 0x04 selects case 4, and the next byte gives 0x05%6 = 5, which reads whences[5] of a 5-element stack array. That is an out-of-bounds read (undefined behavior; ASan reports it).
accepted.alternative_paths: None. The harness's own decoding performs the read before gzseek is called, so no input avoids it once that byte value is chosen.

assumptions: Default ./configure in build.sh defines neither ZLIB_INSECURE nor anything that changes the harness's gzprintf route.
